name: The hot seat
start_line: {chairman} and the board have put you on notice at {club}.

title: {chairman} sets the line
text: The chairman wants it on the table before another game is played: this is the season you keep your job or lose it. The board's goal for the year is the line.

choices.label: Accept the target
choices.result: You shake on it. The goal stands.

choices.label: Argue for a lower one
choices.result: {chairman} hears you out and writes nothing down.

title: Three in a row
text: Three losses running, and every eye in the building is on you. The side is waiting to hear what changes.

choices.label: Change the game plan

effects.why: You dropped the plan the group had trained all summer
You tore up the plan to save the season

choices.result: A new plan is on the whiteboard by Tuesday, and a summer's work on the old one goes with it.

choices.label: Hold the line

effects.why: You backed the group under pressure

choices.result: You tell them the plan is right and the results will come. {chairman} wanted to see a change.

title: A leak from the boardroom
text: Someone on {chairman}'s board has told the papers your job is gone at season's end.

choices.label: Go public
choices.result: You front the cameras and say it to the board's face.

choices.label: Say nothing
choices.result: No comment, and back to work. The players read it in the papers instead.

title: The must-win game
text: {opp} this week. The papers say this is the game that decides your future.

choices.label: Promise the board a win
choices.result: You tell {chairman}: we win this one.

choices.label: Ask to be judged on the season
choices.result: You tell {chairman} one game does not make a season. He wanted a promise.

still_warned.line: Another season on notice. The hot seat stays hot.

survived.line: You survived the hot seat. The board starts next season a little warmer.

name: Board feud
start_line: You and {chairman}'s board are no longer speaking the same language.

title: The football budget
text: {chairman} wants the club's football spending cut, starting now.

choices.label: Accept the cut

effects.why: The football side lost money it needed

choices.result: You find the savings.

choices.label: Fight it
choices.result: You tell the board the cut costs games.

title: The sponsor's favourite
text: A major sponsor wants {name} in the side, and {chairman} has made sure you know it.

choices.label: Pick {first}
choices.result: {name} gets his game. The rooms notice.

choices.label: Refuse
choices.result: Selection stays yours.

title: A board election
text: A challenger is running against {chairman}. Both camps want to know where you stand.

choices.label: Back the challenger
choices.result: You put your name to the other ticket.

choices.label: Stay out of it

effects.why: You kept football out of club politics

choices.result: You tell both camps your job is the football.

won_over.line: The challenger won the vote. The new board is your board.

lost_feud.line: {chairman} held his seat, and remembers who backed the other side.

peace.line: Your feud with the board has settled into an uneasy peace.

name: The protege
start_line: {name} is your project now: the kid you have put your name to.

title: How much does {first} play?
text: {name} has made his mark early. The question is how much senior football he plays this year.

choices.label: Play {first} every week
choices.result: {first} plays every week he is fit.

choices.label: Manage {first}'s games
choices.result: {first} sits out some weeks, and does not enjoy watching.

title: Rivals ask about {first}
text: Two clubs have called about {name}. Word gets back to him that you took the calls.

choices.label: Say {first} is untouchable

effects.why: You told rival clubs he was not for sale

choices.result: You tell both clubs {first} is not for sale.

choices.label: Listen

effects.why: You listened to offers for him

choices.result: You hear the offers. {first} hears that you did.

title: The leadership group
text: {name} has the respect of the young group. Some of the older ones want him to wait his turn.

choices.label: Put {first} in the group

effects.why: You put him in the leadership group

choices.result: {name} joins the leaders.

choices.label: Not yet
choices.result: You tell {first} his time will come. He wanted it now.

title: The next captain
text: The club asks who leads after the current captain. Everyone knows you would say {name}.

choices.label: Name {first} the heir

effects.why: You named him the next captain

choices.result: {name} is the captain-in-waiting.

choices.label: Keep it as it is
choices.result: No change at the top. {first} hears his name was not put forward.

title: {first} names his reason
text: {name}'s new deal is on the table. {first} tells the papers he is staying because of you.

choices.label: Thank {first} in public

effects.why: You thanked him in public for staying

choices.result: A handshake for the cameras.

choices.label: Make it about the team

effects.why: You turned a star's praise back to the group

choices.result: You tell the papers it is about the club.

left.line: {name} has gone. The kid you backed plays his football somewhere else now.

heir.line: {name}, the kid you backed, is now your captain-in-waiting.

made.line: {name} has made it, and you backed him from the start.

name: One year too long
start_line: {name} has {games} games behind him and his body is telling him it is the last year.

title: {first}'s last year?
text: {name} comes to see you. He thinks this is his last season and wants to know what you think.

choices.label: Ask {first} to think about one more

effects.why: You told him you wanted him for another year

choices.result: {first} says he'll decide at season's end.

choices.label: Plan {first}'s send-off
choices.result: You start planning a proper farewell.

title: {first} is struggling
text: {name}'s form has dropped off. The younger ones are pushing for his spot.

choices.label: Keep picking {first}
choices.result: {first} keeps his place. The younger ones keep waiting.

choices.label: Drop {first}

effects.why: You dropped him in his last season
A club great was dropped in his last year

choices.result: {first} takes it badly.

title: {first} has still got it
text: {name} was the hero on the weekend, and the papers want to know if his last season is really his last.

choices.label: Say {first} has earned his say
choices.result: {first} reads it on Monday and stands a little taller.

choices.label: Say the plan has not changed

effects.why: You said his last season is still his last

choices.result: {first} nods, and says nothing.

title: A farewell game
text: {name} asks for one last game in front of the home crowd.

choices.label: Give {first} the game
choices.result: {first} will run out one last time.

choices.label: Say no
choices.result: You tell {first} the side picks itself.

sour_exit.line: {name} has retired. He was dropped in his last season and has not forgotten it.

no_send_off.line: {name} has retired after {games} games, without the farewell game he asked for.

send_off.line: {name} has retired after {games} games, with the send-off you gave him.

one_more.line: {name} has gone round again: one more year.

name: The drought
start_line: {drought} seasons with you in charge and no flag. {chairman} is counting.

title: Flag or bust
text: {chairman} says it out loud: {drought} seasons without a flag is enough.

choices.label: Accept it

effects.why: You said it was flag or bust

choices.result: Flag or bust it is.

choices.label: Ask for time
choices.result: You ask for one more build. {chairman} does not like waiting.

title: All in?
text: Mid-season. The list can push for this year, or keep building for the next three.

choices.label: Go all in on this year

effects.why: You went all in on this season

choices.result: You tell the group it is this year.

choices.label: Keep building

effects.why: You kept building the list

choices.result: You play the long game. {chairman} wanted this year.

title: September again
text: Finals. {drought} seasons of waiting, and the whole club knows it.

choices.label: Lift them for one more step
choices.result: One more week.

choices.label: Keep it calm

effects.why: You kept September calm

choices.result: No speeches. The group trains as it has all year.

broken.line: The drought is over. A flag, at last, with you in charge.

another_miss.line: You said flag or bust, and there is no flag. {chairman}'s board has not forgotten it.

goes_on.line: Still no flag at {club}. The drought goes on.

moved_on.line: You leave {club} without the flag the drought was about.

season_line: {drought} seasons at {club} and still no flag. The drought goes on.

name: The star who wants out
start_line: {name} is unhappy at {club} and wants a move.

title: {first}'s manager calls
text: {name}'s manager says {first} is open to a move, and wants every talk to go through the manager.

choices.label: Meet {first} yourself

effects.why: You came to him yourself

choices.result: You sit down with {first}, no manager in the room.

choices.label: Deal through the manager

effects.why: You only spoke to his manager

choices.result: Phone calls with the manager.

title: What would keep {first}?
text: {first} wants to feel he matters here. You can show him, or start looking at what he would bring in a trade.

choices.label: Tell {first} he's the heart of it
choices.result: {first} hears it, and trains like it.

choices.label: Shop {first}

effects.why: You shopped him to other clubs

choices.result: Calls go out to the other clubs.

title: Stay or go
text: The season is nearly done. {name} wants an answer before the trade period.

choices.label: Ask {first} to stay
choices.result: You ask {first} to stay.

choices.label: Tell {first} he can go
choices.result: You will not stand in {first}'s way. The rest hear that one of their best is free to leave.

left.line: {name} has left {club}. Twice a year now you face him.

sulks.line: {name} stayed, and is still not happy about it.

name: Media darling or villain
start_line: {journalist} is writing about {club} every week now, and about you.

title: A weekly radio spot
text: {journalist}'s station wants you on air every Monday.

choices.label: Take it

effects.why: You took a weekly radio spot

choices.result: Mondays on air. The board likes the coverage, and the players see where your Mondays go.

choices.label: Say no

effects.why: You turned down a radio spot to keep your mind on the club

choices.result: Football first.

title: {journalist} names {first}
text: {journalist} writes that {name} is the problem at {club}.

choices.label: Defend {first}

effects.why: You defended him against the papers

choices.result: You take {journalist} on in public.

choices.label: Agree with {journalist}

effects.why: You agreed with the papers about him

choices.result: You tell {journalist} the criticism is fair.

title: A story leaks
text: {journalist} has a story about the players' night out. It runs tomorrow.

choices.label: Front it yourself

effects.why: You fronted the media for the group

choices.result: You take the questions, and the club's name is in the story all week.

choices.label: Blame the players
choices.result: You hang it on the players. The board is glad the club is clear of it.

villain.line: In {journalist}'s columns you are the villain now. The players have closed ranks.

darling.line: The media love you. The board likes the coverage; some players think you are distracted.

quiet.line: You have gone quiet in the press, and the story has moved on.

name: The rivalry you made
start_line: {club} and {rival_club}: a rivalry made on your watch.

title: {rival_club}'s coach has a go
text: {rival_club}'s coach says your side cannot win the big ones. It is on every back page.

choices.label: Answer back
choices.result: You give it straight back. The board would rather you had stayed out of it.

choices.label: Let it go

effects.why: You let the football do the talking

choices.result: No reply.

title: A call from {rival_club}
text: {rival_club}'s list manager wants to talk about a swap.

choices.label: Hear them out

effects.why: You talked trade with the old enemy

choices.result: You take the call. The group hears you are talking with {rival_club}.

choices.label: Never with them

effects.why: You would not deal with the old enemy

choices.result: Not them. Not ever.

title: {rival_club} in a final
text: A final against {rival_club}. Nothing else this week matters.

choices.label: Fire them up
choices.result: They will run through a wall.

choices.label: Stick to the plan

effects.why: You treated the rival final like any other

choices.result: Same plan, same jobs.

truce.line: {club} and {rival_club} have made a truce of sorts. They do business now.

named.line: {club} against {rival_club} is a rivalry with a name now, and you made it.

name: Family club
start_line: {name} is at {club}: the son of {father}, who played under you.

title: {father}'s boy
text: {name} arrives with his father's name on his back and every old teammate watching.

choices.label: Look after {first}
choices.result: You make sure {first} settles.

choices.label: No favours

effects.why: You gave the father-son no favours

choices.result: {first} gets no favours.

title: {father} in the stands
text: {name} is picked to play. {father} will be in the stands.

choices.label: Ask {father} to present the jumper
choices.result: Father hands son the jumper.

choices.label: Keep it low-key
choices.result: No ceremony. {first} runs out with the rest.

got_away.line: {name}, {father}'s son, has left {club}. The one that got away.

dynasty.line: Father and son, both under you: {name} carries on {father}'s name at {club}.

name: Legacy
start_line: {seasons_coached} seasons and {coach_games} games in the job. Your legacy is being talked about.

title: How to mark it
text: The club wants to mark your milestone before this week's game.

choices.label: Make it about the players
choices.result: You turn the day over to the players.

choices.label: Accept the honour
choices.result: A guard of honour and a speech.

title: Who comes after you?
text: {chairman} asks the question nobody else will: who takes over when you go?

choices.label: Start the handover now

effects.why: You started planning your succession

choices.result: You name your senior assistant as the next coach.

choices.label: Not yet
choices.result: You tell {chairman} there is time. He wanted a name.

successor_ready.line: Your legacy is set, and your successor is named.

coaching_on.line: Your legacy is set. You coach on, with no successor named.

moved_on.line: You leave {club}. Your legacy there is still being talked about.

name: The sack and the way back
start_line: Sacked by {old_club}, you start again at {club}.

title: Why {old_club} let you go
text: Your first press call at {club}, and {journalist} only wants to ask about {old_club}.

choices.label: Go quietly

effects.why: You would not talk about your old club

choices.result: You talk about {club} and nothing else.

choices.label: Speak your mind
choices.result: You say {old_club} gave up on a plan halfway through. It runs on every back page.

title: A call from {former}
text: {former}, who you coached at {old_club}, rings to ask how the new place is treating you.

choices.label: Keep in touch

effects.why: You were still on the phone to your old club's players

choices.result: You talk for an hour. {former} misses the old plan.

choices.label: Keep it short

effects.why: You gave everything to the new group

choices.result: You wish {former} well and hang up. {club} is the job now.

title: {old_club} this week
text: The first game against the club that sacked you. {old_chairman} will be in the box.

choices.label: Say it is just a game
choices.result: You tell the press it is four points like any other.

choices.label: Say it means everything
choices.result: You tell the group this one is for you. They hear it.

sacked_again.line: Sacked by {old_club}, and now by {club} too. The way back has run out of road.

rebuilt.line: One season at {club} and the board's goal is met. {old_club} are a memory now.

settled.line: A first season at {club} is done. The sacking at {old_club} is behind you.

name: Poached
start_line: {suitor} want a new coach, and they want you.

title: {suitor_president} on the phone
text: {suitor_president}, president of {suitor}, rings you at home. He wants a coffee, nothing more, yet.

choices.label: Listen
choices.result: You agree to a coffee. By Friday someone at {club} knows.

choices.label: Hang up
choices.result: You tell {suitor_president} you have a job. {chairman} hears about it and is pleased.

title: {name} asks you straight

text.text: Another club has come calling: {suitor} this time. {name} has been here before with you, and asks if you are going.

text: The rumours have reached the rooms. Your captain {name} asks if you are leaving for {suitor}.

choices.label: Tell {first} the truth

effects.why: You told him the truth about the other club's approach

choices.result: You tell {name} you have met {suitor_president}. He respects it, and the rooms know by the weekend.

choices.label: Deny it

effects.why: You told him there was nothing in it, after you had met the other club

choices.result: You look {name} in the eye and say there is nothing in it. He goes back to training.

choices.label: Tell {first} the truth

effects.why: You told him the truth about the second approach

choices.result: You tell {name} it is {suitor} this time, and that you have met them. He nods. He has heard it before.

choices.label: Deny it

effects.why: You told him there was nothing in another club's approach

choices.result: You say no again. {name} does not look as sure this time.

title: The offer from {suitor}
text: {suitor} put it in writing: a bigger list budget, a longer deal, and the senior job from next season.

choices.label: Take it to {chairman}
choices.result: {chairman} matches it, and does not enjoy doing so.

choices.label: Take the job
choices.result: You sign for {suitor}, to start next season. The rooms know within the week.

choices.label: Say no
choices.result: You thank {suitor_president} and say no.

left.line: You have left {club} for {suitor}. {chairman} will not forget it.

new_deal.line: You stay at {club} on a richer deal, and {chairman}'s board is cooler for it.

loyal.line: {suitor} came for you and went away without you. {club} has a loyal coach.

name: The old-club reunion

start_line.text: {club} against {old_club}, {flag_years_on} years on from the {flag_year} {old_club} premiership you won there.

start_line: {club} against {old_club}: you meet your old club.

title: Grudge match

text.text: {old_club} bring back the {flag_year} premiership side for a lap before the game, {flag_years_on} years on. You coached that side, and now you are in the other box. {journalist} wants a line from you.

text: The papers call {old_club} this week a grudge match. {former}, who you coached there, lines up against you.

choices.label: Tag {former}

effects.why: You planned for the man you knew best

choices.result: You put your best stopper on {former}.

choices.label: Bite back in the press
choices.result: You tell {journalist} you know where the bodies are buried at {old_club}. The board winces.

choices.label: Play it down
choices.result: You say {old_club} are one more side to beat, and leave it there.

title: The handshake

text.text: After the game, {old_chairman} waits by the race with a {flag_year} premiership medal to sign. The cameras are on you both.

text: After the {old_club} game, {old_chairman} waits by the race. The cameras are on you both.

choices.label: Shake {old_chairman}'s hand
choices.result: A handshake, and a word of thanks for the years. It leads the news.

choices.label: Walk past {old_chairman}
choices.result: You walk past {old_chairman} without a word. The cameras get all of it.

remembered.line: You beat {old_club}, and {club} will bring it up at every meeting from now on.

level.line: You and {old_club} finished level. Honours shared.

reconciled.line: {old_club} got the better of the day, but you and {old_chairman} are on speaking terms again.

enjoyed.line: {old_club} got the better of their old coach, and enjoyed every minute of it.

name: The assistant who wants your job
start_line: {assistant}, {club}'s senior assistant, is being talked about for the top job.

title: {assistant} at lunch with {chairman}
text: Someone saw your senior assistant {assistant} at lunch with {chairman}. Nobody told you about it.

choices.label: Confront {assistant}

effects.why: You would not be undermined

choices.result: You ask {assistant} what the lunch was about. He says it was about nothing.

choices.label: Give {assistant} more to do
choices.result: You hand {assistant} the forward line. If he wants the job, he can earn it.

title: {assistant_to} want {assistant}
text: {assistant_to} have offered {assistant} their senior job from next season. He asks what you think.

choices.label: Back {assistant} to go

effects.why: You backed your assistant to take a senior job

choices.result: You tell {assistant} to take it. He will be a friend at {assistant_to}.

choices.label: Ask {assistant} to stay

effects.why: You stood in your assistant's way

choices.result: You ask {assistant} to stay. He thinks it over, and stays. The group knows what it cost him.

took_job.line: You are gone from {club}, and {assistant} has your job.

left_friend.line: {assistant} has gone to coach {assistant_to}, a friend at a rival club.

stayed_loyal.line: {assistant} stays at {club}, loyal to you for now.
